description: In 1874, painters refused by the Salon organized their own exhibition. A critic mocks Monet and unwittingly calls it **impressionism**.

hero.hook: A critical insult, and the first great movement in modern art has a name.

blocks.text: In April **1874**, around thirty artists tired of [[Official Paris show]] opened a private exhibition in the former studio of photographer Nadar. Among the paintings, a misty seascape by **Claude Monet** attracts the mockery of critic Louis Leroy.
By mocking the title *Print, rising sun*, Leroy unwittingly baptized the first great avant-garde movement in modern art. This is how **impressionism** changed the way we look at reality.

In the 19th century, art in France obeyed the **Academy of Fine Arts**. At the top: history painting. The landscape and daily life are considered minor. To exist, a painter must exhibit at the Salon. We require a precise drawing and a smooth surface, without brush marks.

In **1863**, the jury refused more than **3 000** paintings. The emperor **Napoleon III** then authorized the **Salon des Refusés**. The public discovers *Lunch on the grass* by **Édouard Manet**: a naked woman lunches with two men in modern costume. The scandal is immediate.

blocks.caption: Manet shocked the Salon by mixing the nude and contemporary life.

blocks.text: The members of the Salon jury were nicknamed the “firefighters”: their ancient warriors wore helmets reminiscent of those of the Paris firefighters.

Manet refuses the gentle modeling of academics. He paints in frank contrasts. Without calling himself an impressionist, he becomes the figure of this [[avant-garde]] who places color before perfect drawing.

sections.title: Against the Academy: the scandal of 1863

blocks.text: The revolution also involves technology. Before, the painter ground his pigments in the workshop. With the [[paint tubes and outdoors]], he can finally sit outside in front of the pattern. Facing the wind and the sun, he discovers that the color of an object constantly changes depending on the time and the light.

blocks.caption: Monet and his friends painted en plein air to capture the moment.

blocks.text: Monet sometimes rented a small boat converted into a workshop to paint from the middle of the Seine, as close as possible to the reflections.

To capture these moments, they place touches of pure color side by side. From a distance, the viewer's eye mixes these touches. Inspired by the chemist [[Michel-Eugène Chevreul]], they ban black from shadows and prefer [[complementary colors]]: blue in the shadow of an object lit in orange.

Tired of refusals from the Salon, painters from the Batignolles district met at [[Café Guerbois]]. In **1874**, they are organizing their own exhibition. The group brings together **Monet**, **Renoir**, **Pissarro**, **Degas** and **Berthe Morisot**, whose talent stands out despite the prejudices of the time.

blocks.caption: Photographer Nadar's workshop hosts the first impressionist exhibition.

blocks.text: The press is fierce. Leroy speaks of “impressionists” to say: these are only sketches. However, the group also experiments thanks to the [[Japanese prints]]: asymmetrical framing, overhead views. The merchant [[Paul Durand-Ruel]] supports them and conquers the American market. Between 1874 and 1886, eight exhibitions imposed a new idea: painting one's sensation, not a frozen copy of nature.

sections.title: 1874: from an insult to a movement

blocks.text: By asserting that the way of seeing matters more than the subject, the Impressionists paved the way for modern art. Monet will push this logic to the *Water lilies*, where the contours dissolve and announce abstraction. Seurat's [[Neo-Impressionism]] then systematizes the key into points.

events.detail: Manet scandalized with Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe.
events.title: Salon des Refusés

events.detail: At Nadar, Leroy invented the word “impressionists”.
events.title: First independent exhibition

events.detail: The group imposed a new freedom to paint.
events.title: Eighth and final exhibition

blocks.text: Today, these once-mocked paintings are among the most visited in [[Musée d'Orsay]]. The insult became a triumph.
Born from a revolt against the Salon in **1874**, Impressionism made light, free touch and personal sensation the heart of modern painting.

title: The birth of impressionism
